items.headline: Nvidia's board authorized a record $150 billion increase to its share buyback program
items.why: The largest buyback authorization in history signals Nvidia's cash generation can fund both AI infrastructure spending and shareholder returns at once, yet the stock's muted 2% pop and a flat semiconductor ETF show the market treated it as routine rather than a fresh catalyst.

sources.title: NVIDIA Rises 2% as Board Authorizes Record $150B Buyback Increase; AMD and Broadcom Slip

items.headline: Nvidia released an Open Agent Safety Platform aimed at keeping AI agents from acting outside their intended bounds
items.why: A chipmaker building agent-containment tooling on its own initiative suggests the industry expects AI-safety compliance to become a cost of doing business rather than waiting for regulation to force it.

sources.title: Nvidia says it can keep AI models under control — plus, what to do about Boeing's dip

items.headline: Oracle invoked force majeure on a US AI data center project after local officials delayed the power permits it needed
items.why: The clause is meant for acts of god, not permitting delays, and using it exposes how thin the financial and insurance structure behind the AI buildout is if any single piece — power, permits, or a lease term — slips.

sources.title: Oracle force majeure on US data center showcases AI infrastructure risks

items.headline: Broadcom's custom AI chip revenue grew 221% year-over-year to $16.7 billion in the quarter, with shipments up 3.5x
items.why: Custom silicon cutting inference costs 40-60% versus GPUs gives hyperscalers a real reason to diversify away from Nvidia, and Broadcom trading at a discount to both Nvidia and AMD despite comparable growth is the market still catching up to that shift.

sources.title: Not Nvidia, Not AMD. Broadcom's Custom Silicon Business Is Quietly Becoming an AI Chip Powerhouse

items.headline: Bitcoin and ether dropped after Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Crypto is trading as a risk-off casualty of the Gulf standoff rather than a hedge against it, falling alongside a stronger dollar and higher yields the same way equities and gold did.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Monday, September 28, 2026: Bitcoin loses ground after Trump rejects Iran's 7-day plan

items.headline: Bitcoin and ether surged to January levels after $770 million in short positions were liquidated in 24 hours
items.why: Roughly 85% of that liquidation total came from shorts getting squeezed, which means much of the rally was mechanical short-covering rather than fresh buying conviction, a distinction that matters for how fast it can reverse.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Tuesday, September 22, 2026: Crypto prices continue to surge to prices last seen in January

items.headline: US spot Solana ETFs pulled in a record $188 million in a single week, with Bitwise capturing two-thirds of it
items.why: All seven Solana funds gained inflows even while SOL itself sits 60% below its prior peak, which reads as institutional managers building a position at a discount rather than chasing a rally.

sources.title: Solana ETFs draw record $188 million in a week as Bitwise takes two-thirds of inflows

items.headline: Exchange Bitget began restoring withdrawals after a $388 million exploit it suspects was carried out by a state-backed North Korean group
items.why: The attacker used stolen credentials from a third-party security vendor rather than a flaw in Bitget's own code, which is the same supply-chain pattern behind several of the largest crypto hacks this year and one exchanges have struggled to close off.

sources.title: Bitget starts phased withdrawal resumption following $388 million exploit

items.headline: Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but both sides said talks would resume this week
items.why: A rejected offer that both sides still call a step toward talks is a different risk profile than a rejection that ends negotiations outright, and markets have been pricing the Gulf premium based on which of those two paths is more likely.

sources.title: Live Updates: Iran says Trump must choose between war or diplomacy as talks resume

items.headline: The US and China extended their trade truce two months to January 10, cutting tariffs on $60 billion of goods and opening an AI-incident communication channel
items.why: Publishing the actual product list — US farm goods and wood products for Chinese appliances and toys — turns last week's summit headline into something with enforceable detail, which is the follow-through investors said the truce needed to be credible.

sources.title: China says US trade truce extension creates space to advance talks

items.headline: Fed funds futures now imply a greater than 60-70% chance of an October rate hike, with the October 2 jobs report seen as decisive
items.why: Markets have flipped from debating whether the Fed is done hiking to pricing a hike as the base case, so a jobs report anywhere near the 100,000 consensus removes the last reason to doubt it.

sources.title: Jobs Report, Inflation Data to Test US Rate Path, Economic Strength

items.headline: Gold fell to $4,189 an ounce, its lowest level since August 5 and down 3.1% for the week
items.why: Gold selling off at the same time Iran tensions were escalating is the tell that rate expectations, not geopolitics, are driving metals right now — a stronger dollar and higher real yields are outweighing gold's usual safe-haven bid.

sources.title: Gold prices today, Monday, September 28, 2026: Gold prices slump as Iran tensions and oil prices rise

items.headline: Silver tumbled below $62 an ounce as the odds of an October Fed hike climbed past 70%
items.why: Silver is falling faster than gold on the same rate story because it carries more industrial-demand sensitivity, making it the more volatile read on how seriously the market is taking the hike odds.

sources.title: Silver prices today, Monday, September 28, 2026: Silver prices slump as oil prices and higher-rate expectations rise

items.headline: Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West oil pipeline after a two-week shutdown from drone damage, though full 4 million barrel-a-day capacity is still six to eight weeks out
items.why: A restart at partial capacity keeps Saudi supply constrained for another one to two months even as the headline reads as de-escalation, which is why oil didn't fall in lockstep with the good news.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia's key oil pipeline is restarting after nearly two weeks of drone damage

items.headline: The S&P 500 closed at 7,681 on Monday, down about 0.8% in a broad selloff where no sector offered shelter
items.why: Rising Treasury yields repricing both growth and value stocks at once, rather than a rotation out of one and into the other, is what a genuine valuation reset looks like as opposed to ordinary sector churn.

sources.title: S&P 500 Closes at 7,681 as Rising Treasury Yields Hit Every Sector

items.headline: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.2% by Monday, up from 5.17% the prior Friday and its highest level in roughly two decades
items.why: A multi-week grind higher rather than a single-day spike is the more durable kind of yield move, and it's the direct mechanical driver behind the equity and gold selloffs happening alongside it.

sources.title: Stock Market Today (Sept. 28, 2026): Dow, S&P, Nasdaq updates

items.headline: Only healthcare, staples, and energy closed higher on Monday while over 65% of S&P 500 stocks fell
items.why: A retreat into the market's three classic defensive sectors while two-thirds of names decline is textbook risk-off positioning, distinct from the narrow AI-led rallies that have driven most of this year's gains.

sources.title: Stock Market Today (Sept. 28, 2026): Dow, S&P, Nasdaq updates
